The user wants to close out a rejected invoice.

The disposition should be return_to_vendor. F2 is a stock shortfall, which falls under quantities over what we can accept. Void is reserved for fraud or duplicate data.

The audit log should cite the finding IDs in two or three sentences. The vendor email must be brief and polite. It should state the exact quantities that need correction without revealing internal stock levels or fraud suspicions.

F1 is a date oddity. The vendor email must name each problem with its numbers. The corrected invoice needs the due date changed from January 30 to Net 30.

The vendor email cannot specify a replacement quantity because the exact stock level is internal. It should only state that 20 GadgetX exceeds our accepted limit and request a corrected invoice with an acceptable quantity.

The vendor email should ask them to confirm a lower quantity rather than stating the exact stock level. The due date must be changed from January 30 to Net 30 terms. There is uncertainty about whether F1 belongs in the vendor email since it is only a warning, not the reject reason.

The vendor email should include both findings, since each is a problem on the document. The audit reasoning may cite stock levels because it is internal; the vendor email must not reveal them. The disposition is return_to_vendor.
